Simple forecasting methods often produce more accurate forecasts than complex methods

Combine vs. identify and fit single model that describes the data generating process

“Almost all prediction intervals from [classical] time series models are too narrow. This
is a well-known phenomenon and arises because they do not account for all sources of
uncertainty.Hyndman, Koehler, Snyder, & Grose (2002)measured the size of the problem by
computing the actual coverage percentage of the prediction intervals on test data, and found
that for ETS models, nominal 95% intervals may only provide coverage between 71%
and 87%. The difference is due to missing sources of uncertainty.”
At least four sources of uncertainty in forecasting using time series models:
1. Random error term
2. Parameter estimates
3. Choice of model for the historical data
4. Continuation of the historical data generating process into the future
Model-driven prediction intervals for time series models such as ETS → typically only
account for the first of these sources of uncertainty
